overview: The Medford School Committee is the governing body for the Medford Public Schools district, responsible for setting educational policies, adopting operating and capital budgets, overseeing superintendent leadership, and directing district-wide facilities planning. Across the 87 meetings held between December 2023 and October 2026, the committee navigated leadership transitions, resolved operational budget deficits through local override appropriations, and advanced major infrastructure investments including HVAC replacements and a comprehensive high school building project. The body also routinely updated academic graduation standards, student behavior and non-discrimination policies, and expanded after-school and career technical education programs. At its most recent meeting, the committee reviewed strategic planning community survey results alongside the Lynch Leadership Academy and considered draft guidelines for an elementary school intra-district reassignment policy.

threads.name: Medford Comprehensive High School Building Project
threads.summary: Following acceptance of Medford High School into the Massachusetts School Building Authority core program eligibility phase, the committee established the building committee structure, project goals, and online presence [M02#5, M06#5, M07#4, M07#7]. The body appointed community and administrative members, approved a feasibility study agreement for a 1,395-student enrollment cap, and hired Left Field as Owner's Project Manager [M12#8, M43#7, M51#5]. As educational plans and space summaries advanced, the committee adjusted options to navigate a 1967 DCR deed restriction barring construction on Edgley Field and refined submissions regarding sustainability certifications, vocational viability, and non-high school program spaces [M56#6, M76#2, M79#3, M81#7, M82#1, M83#7]. The committee most recently updated the building committee's membership for the schematic design phase [M84#9].

threads.name: Superintendent transitions and evaluation
threads.summary: After evaluating goals and negotiating contracts with Superintendent Marice Edouard-Vincent through 2024, the committee accepted her departure and appointed Assistant Superintendent Suzanne Galusi as Interim Superintendent [M03#8, M22#2, M38#2, M40#3]. Dr. Galusi presented transition priorities, completed an induction framework, and underwent an annual performance evaluation [M41#2, M62#5, M67#6]. In February 2026, the committee voted to appoint Dr. Galusi as the permanent superintendent and later approved a three-year contract [M68#4, M74#6]. The committee subsequently aligned the superintendent evaluation schedule with the academic year and approved Dr. Galusi's 2026–2027 district goals [M81#11, M85#6].

threads.name: District operating budget and override funding
threads.summary: Mid-year in fiscal year 2024, the district confronted an initial $2.5 million deficit, which was remediated down to $216,000 using encumbrance adjustments, capital funds, and postponed spending [M06#4, M09#5]. The committee submitted a level-service FY25 budget request and adopted an eight-phase budget schedule before approving a $77.75 million operating budget [M16#9, M18#9, M20#7]. Following voter approval of Questions 7 and 8 ballot overrides, the committee approved a supplemental budget appropriation to restore positions and fund collective bargaining reserves [M27#8, M35#7, M40#7]. Budget reviews for FY26 and FY27 addressed inflation and structural deficits, concluding with the committee's approval of the FY27 budget closing a remaining gap of $833,398 [M46#2, M72#3, M81#4].

threads.name: School HVAC and facilities improvements
threads.summary: The committee initiated major building system upgrades by approving an estimated $15 to $20 million decarbonization HVAC project for Andrews and McGlynn middle schools, paired with a policy restriction on fossil-fuel facility equipment [M14#6, M14#13]. It later approved $5 million in initial design borrowing, authorized construction management at risk, and approved a final $25.77 million bond recommendation for the middle schools [M35#6, M39#6, M48#7]. Concurrently, after receiving an assessment identifying $83.7 million in district-wide repair needs, the body submitted MSBA Accelerated Repair statements and approved a $22.7 million schematic design for HVAC electrification and roof work at Roberts Elementary [M46#1, M62#3, M81#5, M84#4]. The committee also granted specific exceptions permitting natural gas-powered appliance replacements [M25#9, M86#4].

threads.name: Elementary enrollment capacity and redistricting planning
threads.summary: Severe overcrowding emerged at Roberts Elementary School, leading to staff and committee proposals for strategic space planning and possible redistricting [M25#8, M26#6, M49#4]. To relieve short-term pressure, the committee relocated preschool classrooms from Roberts to Missituk Elementary and created a space planning task force [M54#6, M54#7]. Following an external space utilization study, the committee reviewed middle school reconfiguration models (such as grades 5–6 and 7–8 spans) but tabled immediate restructuring and later formally delayed any 5–8 grade reconfiguration to 2028 [M63#5, M64#5, M83#4]. The body subsequently took up a draft policy establishing guidelines and criteria for elementary school student reassignments [M59#11, M87#5].

threads.name: Student transportation operations and safety
threads.summary: Driven by driver shortages and route disruptions under the Eastern Bus contract, the committee surveyed community needs, examined late busing, and addressed safety risks highlighted by students [M10#4, M11#1, M25#12, M31#4]. The committee authorized a new five-year agreement with Eastern Bus, initiated an electric bus study, and requested city adoption of automated stop-arm camera enforcement [M55#4, M58#8]. To improve onboard behavior and route reliability, the district implemented a tiered bus monitoring plan deploying paraprofessionals [M60#5, M61#6]. Student representatives recently reported on the successful implementation of high school late bus service expanding extracurricular access [M87#4].

threads.name: Graduation standards and academic policies
threads.summary: Following statewide voter passage of ballot Question 2 removing the MCAS competency requirement for high school graduation, the committee formally amended Policy IKF to replace the state test barrier with aligned local coursework completion [M43#3, M45#7]. It further refined Policy IKF to expand flexibility for health and physical education requirements and protect commencement participation for students receiving certificates of completion [M48#6, M49#3, M54#4]. The committee formally rescinded obsolete MCAS policy language and later approved an MCAS late-entry testing schedule pilot for high school grade cohorts [M55#9, M71#4].

threads.name: Career and technical education expansion and admissions
threads.summary: The committee supported expanding vocational programming during the MSBA core project review, subsequently modifying timelines and removing veterinary science from its state Chapter 74 expansion submissions [M16#8, M45#6]. Facing enrollment caps and high demand, the committee adopted a straight lottery-based admissions policy for oversubscribed Chapter 74 programs and updated the policy following state feedback [M60#3, M61#4, M73#3]. It also approved updated Chapter 74 viability documentation for the MSBA and reviewed a vocational honors pilot allowing students to earn honors credit through co-op employment or capstone projects [M82#1, M85#4].
